newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel-PLO meeting in doubt over settlement 'pause'.
newsitem.headline: Israel-PLO meeting in doubt over settlement 'pause'.

text.p: An Israeli peace team refused to leave for talks with the PLO in Cairo on Sunday, demanding Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority retract statements Israel had accepted a "pause" in Jewish settlement building.

Israel and the PLO agreed on Saturday to revive the talks after two months. But Israel reacted swiftly to statements on Sunday by PLO officials that its agreement in principle to a vague "pause" in settlement construction had cleared the way.

"We told Egypt the Israeli delegation will not be able to go to Cairo until there is an unequivocal denial from the Palestinian Authority that will make clear that Israel did not give any commitment to the Palestinians in order to conduct the meeting in Cairo," Israeli spokesman Shai Bazak told Reuters.

"The delegation is waiting at this time in Jerusalem until there is a denial. I make clear again that no commitment was given to stop the settlements or the building on Har Homa," said Bazak, spokesman for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Israel's talks with the PLO have been in crisis since the Jewish state broke ground three months ago on the 6,500-unit Jewish settlement of Har Homa on an Arab East Jerusalem hill Palestinians call Jabal Abu Ghneim. Construction continued on Sunday.
The meeting had been due to begin at 1400 GMT in Cairo.

Arafat's spokesman Marwan Kanafani sparked the disagreement on Sunday when he told Reuters from Cairo of Israel's "acceptance in principle of a 'pause' in settlement activities". He said this had cleared the way for a meeting.
PLO officials said the meaning of a "pause" was vague.
Bazak said Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh, a member of the Israeli team, had called Egyptian peace envoy Osama al-Baz by phone to inform him Israel would stay home because of Kanafani's remarks.

Israeli officials insisted Netanyahu's right-wing government remained committed to building Jewish settlements on occupied land in the West Bank, including in Arab East Jerusalem, as well as in the Gaza Strip.
Netanyahu's 66-54 majority in parliament could crumble if he stops Jewish settlement backed by religious and right-wing legislators in his government.
More than 130,000 Jews live in settlements scattered throughout the West Bank and Gaza, areas captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war and home to more than two million Palestinians.
Egypt has intensified its mediation role in the three-month-old crisis since a summit between President Hosni Mubarak and Netanyahu last month.

Diplomatic sources said Egypt was pushing a five-point plan which included a freeze on any change in the status of Jerusalem and a ban on Jewish settlement building in the West Bank for "a sufficient period". In return the Palestinians would give a firm commitment to address Israel's security demands.
